thread:
IncidentBot: PAGING: Elevated p99/tail latency for streaming in eu-west2. Symptom: streaming stalls + connection resets. Metrics: p99 generation latency spike 9s -> 12s, increased TLS handshake failures and SYN retransmits. Affected AZs: azb->azc interzone paths. Impact: some customer streaming sessions reset (partial). Severity: potential Sev2.

sara (oncall): ack, I'm on it. tagging @mike and @ryan.

mike (infra): looking at NAT and conntrack. seeing nat-gw-eu-west2-01 with ephemeral port exhaustion spikes around 2481233200..2481234000. conntrack counters high, many TIME_WAIT entries.

ellen (prod-eng): customer reports from AcmeHealth: repeated disconnects for long-lived streams. They saw EOF and reconnect loops.

ryan (network): adding: interzone routing table for azb->azc flapped a few times in the 10m window, DNS latencies in eu-west2 spiked to 200-400ms. suspect hairpinning + NAT egress causing queueing.

sara (oncall): status: assign roles. @mike infra to mitigate NAT, @ryan network to check routing, @ellen customer comms. Creating incident ticket.

oncall-bot: Created incident INC-20260315-891 and paged escalation path.

mike (infra): quick checks: `sudo ss -s` shows high established sockets. nat-gw egress ports near limit. Managed NAT provider reported transient scaling delay. We can try temporary route shift to prefer local NAT in azc/azb while we scale.

ryan (network): running a controlled route preference change to avoid cross-AZ hairpin. Command (internal router):

```
# prefer local-nat for EU region traffic
rtrctl set-preference --region eu-west2 --prefer-local-nat=true --pct 20
```

Applying progressive rollout (20% -> 50% -> 100%). I'll watch for packet loss.

ellen (prod-eng): customer-facing note drafted for status page: "Degraded streaming in EU region — we are mitigating increased connection resets and latency. Some sessions may see brief disconnects." Shall I publish?

sara (oncall): publish now.

ellen (prod-eng): posted to status.redwood.com and sent targeted note to AcmeHealth SRE. They responded: "Thanks, any ETA?" I replied we're rolling a routing mitigation now; will update in 10m.

mike (infra): temporary sysctl tweaks to reduce TIME_WAIT and increase ephemeral range prepared but requires change on managed NAT. Asking ops approval. Meanwhile I increased NAT pool on our side where possible and cleared stale conntrack entries: `conntrack -F` on affected proxies.

ryan (network): rollout at 50% shows p99 down from ~9s to ~2.1s and streaming stalls reduced. DNS latencies trending down. Packet loss on azb->azc path reduced from 3% -> 0.4%. Good signal.

mike (infra): still seeing TLS handshake backlog on edge-proxy-2 (accept queue depth high). Might be accept(2) backlog + slow TCP handshakes causing queueing. I'll trigger a rolling restart of edge-proxy-2 after draining traffic.

sara (oncall): approve rolling restart, coordinate with @ryan to keep traffic shifting.

ryan (network): draining edge-proxy-2 via LB: `lbctl drain edge-proxy-2 && sleep 45 && lbctl up edge-proxy-2`. initiating now.

mike (infra): restarted edge-proxy-2, accept queue cleared; TLS handshakes failures drop to baseline. p99 now ~700ms for streamed responses; p95 stable ~120ms.

ellen (prod-eng): AcmeHealth confirms their ingestion resumed and errors dropped to near 0. They've unpaused jobs.

sara (oncall): summary so far: routing rollback -> prefer local NAT; conntrack pruning; NAT pool adjustments; drained + restarted edge-proxy; net result p99 improved from 9s -> 0.7s and streaming stalls largely resolved.

mike (infra): created followup Jira RN-1122: "eu-west2 interzone NAT & routing hardening" with action items: split per-AZ NATs, increase ephemeral port ranges, add conntrack alerting and autoscale for managed NAT. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RN-1122

ryan (network): added runbook item to detect route-table flaps and auto-preference fallback. Also captured tcpdump on nat-gw-eu-west2-01 and uploaded to s3: s3://redwood-ops/inc/2481234567/pcap.tgz

sara (oncall): prepping handoff to night oncall @jason in 30m. Please add monitoring windows and watch p99 for 2h.

jason (night-oncall): ack, I'll pick this up in the shift. Will keep eyes on streaming p99 and TLS errors for 2 hours.

ellen (prod-eng): posting quick postmortem draft to #postmortems with timeline + mitigations. Requested owner: mike (infra).

mike (infra): I will own the postmortem. immediate remediation done, long-term remediation planned in RN-1122. Note: need vendor escalation with managed NAT provider about scaling latency.

oncall-bot: Incident INC-20260315-891 marked resolved by sara (oncall). Severity: Sev2. Root cause: combination of interzone route flaps and NAT ephemeral port pressure leading to queueing and TLS handshake backlog.

sara (oncall): closing the paging; leaving incident open in Jira for remediation. Thanks all for quick response. :rocket:

ellen (prod-eng): couple of follow-ups: add telemetry for accept queue fullness on edge proxies, add quick failover policy for NAT route preferences, and run chaos test for interzone routing next sprint.

mike (infra): added all to RN-1122; will schedule vendor call and config changes next week.

jason (night-oncall): will watch overnight and report if any regressions.

sara (oncall): signoff: incident mitigated, customer impact reduced to minimal, followups assigned.

IncidentBot: Log summary saved to s3://redwood-ops/incident-logs/2481234567/summary.log"
